verdict.rationale: Cursor's docs say Bugbot reads existing PR comments to avoid duplicate suggestions and build on prior feedback, and they list an 'Automatically Learn Rules' toggle, which together suggest it can take pushback into account. A hands-on community report concretely contradicts this: after the user argued against Bugbot's fix and reverted it, Bugbot returned the exact same original recommendation. Missing for 10: documentation of how pushback on a comment is captured and turned into learned rules, evidence that rejected feedback stays suppressed across later reviews, and independent corroboration that the learning works.

support.subject: As a developer, I can push back on a bad review comment and the reviewer learns — it stops repeating the same rejected feedback

citations.quote: reads connected PR comments (top-level and inline) to avoid duplicate suggestions and build on prior feedback
